correctness.rationale: All hypotheses and normalizations were reconstructed. The hypersurface-area measure of a Cartesian product is supported, apart from null multiple-boundary sets, on normals belonging to a single factor. Thus projection-product replacement preserves the first mixed volumes while monotonicity bounds the mixed term. The product Minkowski-volume polynomial yields the exact coefficients with factors \(n\) and \(n(n-1)\). For \(d_i\ge2\), the within-factor coefficient obeys \(c_i\le ((d_i-1)/d_i)\beta_{d_i}(K_i)a_i b_i\); for one-dimensional factors it is zero. Nonnegative bilinear weights yield the stated maximum. Cross-factor segments attain its first candidate and same-factor near-optimizers attain all other candidates; thickening handles full-dimensional test conventions. An independent exact-arithmetic finite verifier returned VERIFY_OK 8054, but the analytic argument, not those finite tests, proves the general theorem.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The universal estimates n (arbitrary tests) and two (zonoid tests) do not imply the sharper \(n/(n-1)\) coefficient for general tests on products when \(n>2\), and coefficient-one characterization gives only that nonsimplices have coefficient exceeding one. The exact product law additionally identifies factorwise maxima and all sharp cross-factor witnesses.

originality.rationale: The exact max-type reduction for all nontrivial Cartesian products is compared with the closest four primary texts, including a 2013 mixed-discriminant analogue with the same numerical constant, the 2015 planar and zonoid Bézout results, and a 2017 universal convex-body estimate. The 2013 paper expressly says the same mixed-volume inequality fails for arbitrary bodies above the plane; none of the inspected primary results states the sharp factorwise product law for arbitrary test bodies. Product-of-simplices special cases may admit older multi-homogeneous derivations; no novelty is attributed to those isolated consequences. Historical equivalence remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: Older or differently named tensorization theorems for the Bézout ratio may not be indexed; a negative literature search does not establish global uniqueness.
The public 2026 Banach--Mazur stability record was available only as an indexed summary during comparison; its scientific claim is distinct and not a decisive unresolved coverage comparison.
Classical multihomogeneous Bézout results may contain independent special-case estimates for products of simplices, so no novelty is assigned to that isolated consequence.
No human or independent scientific audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The optimal constant of a natural affine-invariant inequality is unknown for general fixed convex bodies. The result gives a complete exact max formula on the broad, structurally natural class of nontrivial Cartesian products, reveals different extremal mechanisms (between-factor and inside-factor), and settles every product built from arbitrary planar convex factors and segments with optimal coefficient \(n/(n-1)\). These are infinitely many continuous shape families in arbitrary dimension, not a routine one-body numerical entry. The contrast with the general n bound and the zonoid-test bound 2 provides mathematical motivation for determining the sharp smaller constant.
